prov_cung_tinh.name: Củng Tinh
prov_cung_tinh.lore: Open high plain more than a thousand metres up, cut by a river and dotted with mountain lakes. Herders and a few barley farmers live around the abbey of Củng Tinh Quán, which keeps the star-iron mine at Vẫn Tinh. On still nights the star-readers watch Tinh Lạc Hồ, and the herders keep their fires low so as not to spoil the water's stars.

prov_p140.name: Mộc Hương
prov_p140.lore: River forest and steppe on the northern edge of the plain, grown with scented incense trees. Its woodcutters cut only fallen and dying trees for the Pivot Hall's fires. Spirit horses run wild on the steppe beyond the groves, and the villagers keep well away from their herd.

prov_p141.name: Thụ Âm
prov_p141.lore: Dry steppe with a little forest and badland along a river, around the great tree of Thụ Âm Thôn. Its people keep goats and grow millet on the river flats. The roots of the great tree are said to reach down to an Earth and Wood vein under the steppe.

prov_p52.name: Thiên Quyền
prov_p52.lore: Mountain flanks and grassy steppe at the foot of Thiên Xu Tông's seat, around the market of Thiên Quyền Thị. Traders, weighers and carters live by the market, and a copper mine above it supplies the bronze for the market's weights. Every road to the seat passes through here, and every load is weighed.

prov_p81.name: Thạch Kiều
prov_p81.lore: Rolling steppe and desert edge on a river, around Thạch Kiều Thành, the first city of the heart. Caravans from four coasts meet here, and the farms on the river flats feed the city. Out on the desert edge lie the buried halls of Minh Sa Các, a small sect the sand took back.

prov_thien_xu.name: Thiên Xu
prov_thien_xu.lore: The bare mountain of Thiên Xu Tông's seat and its green slopes, the heart of the Bắc Thần Phúc Địa over Tử Vi Mạch. No mortal village stands inside the seat's wards; servants and disciples live on its terraces. Array stone for the sect's formations is quarried just below the halls.

prov_r14_1.name: Hồng Quả
prov_r14_1.lore: Forested hills rising to bare mountain on the northern edge of the plain. Its people pick hawthorn berries and make them into sweets and medicine for the markets of Thiên Quyền. A Metal vein on the mountain above draws cultivators of sword arts.

prov_r14_10.name: Phong Thực Nguyên
prov_r14_10.lore: Steppe and grey badland worn into pillars and hollows by the wind, around the sulphur pans of Lưu Hoàng Khoáng. No one lives here; sulphur workers come in shifts. A Fire vein breathes under the badland floor, and its heat keeps the snow off the pans.

prov_r14_11.name: Xích Thổ Nguyên
prov_r14_11.lore: Red badlands, steppe and mountain around the cinnabar terraces of Thần Sa Khoáng. Miners and alchemists come and go, but no village stands here. A warm red spring in the steppe is where the miners wash off the cinnabar dust.

prov_r14_12.name: Thanh Khoa
prov_r14_12.lore: High plain of lakes and a river between Củng Tinh Quán and the Pivot's mountain, at the edge of the blessed land. Its people grow highland barley and keep yaks along the river. Quartz from its mountain mine goes to the Pivot's formation masters, and an old fort above the river once guarded the seat's west road.

prov_r14_13.name: Khung Lư
prov_r14_13.lore: Wide steppe and mountain east of the Pivot's seat. Its people are herders who live in felt yurts and move with the grass, wintering by a warm spring in the hills. On a mountain shoulder stands the empty tower of Khuy Thiên Các, star-readers who joined Củng Tinh Quán long ago.

prov_r14_14.name: Thiên Lang Lĩnh
prov_r14_14.lore: Mountains, forest and high plain on the western edge of Thiên Tuyền, named for the bright Wolf Star that rises over them in winter. No village stands here; gold-washers work its streams in summer. Its pine-shadowed peak is a landmark from the plain.

prov_r14_15.name: Thiên Cơ Lĩnh
prov_r14_15.gloss: Ridge of the Heavenly Pearl Star
prov_r14_15.lore: High mountains south of the Pivot's seat, named for the third star of the Dipper. Iron sand is washed from its gullies and carried up to the seat's smithies. Its peak of the nine luminaries is where the Pivot's disciples go to sit alone.

prov_r14_16.name: Đẩu Bính Lĩnh
prov_r14_16.lore: Mountain, steppe and grassland south of the market, curving like the handle of the Dipper on the map. No one lives here now. A beacon fort on its slopes once passed warnings from the borders to the seat.

prov_r14_17.name: Thiên Thị Lĩnh
prov_r14_17.lore: A short mountain ridge and steppe named for the star enclosure of the Heavenly Market. Caravans cross its saddle between Thiên Quyền and the southern mines. It has no village, only a few herders' shelters.

prov_r14_18.name: Ngũ Xa Lĩnh
prov_r14_18.lore: Mountains with grassy and steppe valleys, named for the five-chariot constellation. Agate is dug in its rock, and an old stockade where soldiers once farmed lies empty in a grassy valley. Herders summer their flocks here.

prov_r14_19.name: Bi Phong Lĩnh
prov_r14_19.lore: Bare mountains and badlands on the western rim of the plain, near the old ramparts of Cố Lũy and the poisoned waste of Chiết Kích Nguyên. No one lives here. The wind moans in its gaps, and herders say it moans loudest in the season the battle was fought.

prov_r14_2.name: Hoàng Bách Lĩnh
prov_r14_2.lore: Forest and mountain in the north-west, grown with cork trees whose yellow inner bark is a dye and a medicine. Bark peelers come up in summer and dry their bark on racks. No one stays through the winter.

prov_r14_20.name: Tàn Kỳ Lĩnh
prov_r14_20.lore: Mountain, steppe and badland on the edge of Chiết Kích Nguyên, where the War of Broken Halberds ended in 803. No one lives here; alum is dug by day crews who leave by dusk. Shepherds will not cross its upper slopes, which run down toward the miasma.

prov_r14_21.name: Mao Ngưu
prov_r14_21.lore: High plain at the western edge of Thiên Tuyền, near the ramparts of Cố Lũy. Its people herd yaks and sheep on the short grass. A hot spring in the hills is where Quý Trường Kích's soldiers washed their armour in the five years they held the ramparts.

prov_r14_22.name: Tô Du
prov_r14_22.lore: High plain and badland along a river in the south-west of the plain. Its herders make yak butter and cheese and sell them at Thạch Kiều. Lapis is cut in its mountains, and the walls of an old remount fort stand empty on the plain.

prov_r14_23.name: Thạch Ốc
prov_r14_23.lore: High plain, steppe and badland along a river south of the Pivot's mountain. Its people build their houses of stone against the wind and farm barley and peas on the river flats. A Metal vein on the steppe is said to lie where one of the falling stars of the Wild Age struck.

prov_r14_24.name: Xa Ngưu
prov_r14_24.lore: Steppe and mountain along a river on the south side of the plain. Its people raise oxen for the caravans and the Pivot's carts. Amethyst is dug in the mountain above, and a Metal vein of high winds sits on a bare steppe shoulder.

prov_r14_25.name: Hồ Dương
prov_r14_25.lore: Steppe and desert edge along a river, its banks lined with desert poplars. Its people farm the river flats and boil salt from a warm brine spring in the hills. Caravans bound for the desert water here.

prov_r14_26.name: Hôi Vụ Hoang
prov_r14_26.lore: Mountains and high plain around Chiết Kích Nguyên, the plain poisoned by the battle of 803, and the Vạn Cốt Trủng that rose over the dead. No one lives here, and shepherds will not cross it. Thiên Xu's patrols walk its rim and do not go in.

prov_r14_27.name: Thạch Điền
prov_r14_27.lore: High plain, forest and badland in the far south-west, more than fourteen hundred metres up. Its people farm small terraced fields walled with stone and keep goats. A sulphur spring and a soapstone pit give them something to sell.

prov_r14_28.name: Bách Linh
prov_r14_28.lore: Steppe and high plain along a river in the south of Thiên Tuyền, loud with larks in spring. Its people herd sheep and farm the river flats. A Wood vein in a forested fold and a silver sand mine in the mountain lie nearby.

prov_r14_29.name: Thạch Dương
prov_r14_29.lore: High steppe and mountain on the southern rim, under the hawk cliffs of Thương Ưng Đài. Its herders keep goats on the stony grass. Green jade is cut in the mountain above, and young cultivators climb the hawk cliffs for chicks.

prov_r14_3.name: Xuyên Vân Lĩnh
prov_r14_3.lore: Forest and steep mountain in the north of the plain, whose peaks stand above the cloud on most mornings. No one lives here; woodcutters from the plain climb up for timber in summer. Its white hairpin peak can be seen from Mộc Hương Thôn.

prov_r14_30.name: Mã Nãi
prov_r14_30.lore: Steppe, high plain and badland along a river in the south. Its herders keep horses and brew fermented mare's milk, which they trade at Thạch Kiều. An Earth vein lies under the wide steppe nearby.

prov_r14_31.name: Hoang Thành Nguyên
prov_r14_31.lore: Steppe, mountain and desert in the south-east of Thiên Tuyền, with no village left. Its name comes from the walls of Lục Hợp Thành on a mountain shelf, a caravan city emptied after the earthquake of 912. Herders pass through in spring and avoid the old streets.

prov_r14_32.name: Hoàng Sa Nguyên
prov_r14_32.lore: Desert and dry steppe along a river on the south-eastern edge. No one lives here but a few river fishermen in summer. Golden scorpions as big as dogs hide in its sand, and caravans do not camp in the open.

prov_r14_33.name: Du Mục
prov_r14_33.lore: Steppe, mountain and high plain in the south of the plain, where herders move with the grass. They winter by a warm spring in the hills. Saltpetre is scraped from a cave in the mountain and sold to Thiên Xu for fire powders.

prov_r14_34.name: Liệp Ưng
prov_r14_34.lore: Steppe and mountain in the south of the plain. Its people fly hawks and falcons for hares and foxes and sell trained birds at Thạch Kiều. A frost-headed peak stands over their village.

prov_r14_35.name: Nam Đẩu Lĩnh
prov_r14_35.lore: High mountains on the southern rim of Thiên Tuyền, named for the southern constellation that faces the northern Dipper. No one lives here; a few crews dig rubies in summer. Its peak of the longevity star is climbed by old cultivators near the end of their years.

prov_r14_36.name: Vọng Dương Lĩnh
prov_r14_36.lore: High mountains on the south-eastern rim, whose seaward side drops to the coast. From its grassy summit the far water can be seen. Azurite is dug in its flanks, and no village stands here.

prov_r14_4.name: Tùng Nhân
prov_r14_4.lore: Steppe, mountain and forest north of the Pivot's mountain. Its people gather pine nuts from the forests and herd sheep on the steppe. Its lotus-shaped peak is the first thing travellers from the north see of the seat's mountains.

prov_r14_5.name: Đương Quy
prov_r14_5.lore: Mountain, high plain and forest in the north-west. Its people grow and dig angelica root and other herbs for the alchemists of the plain. Dark ore is dug in the mountain above the village.

prov_r14_6.name: Bắc Cực Lĩnh
prov_r14_6.lore: High bare mountains just north of the Pivot's seat, under the pole star in the sky. No one lives here but the seat's watchmen. Gold is dug in a small mine for the sect's own use.

prov_r14_7.name: Hoàng Kỳ
prov_r14_7.lore: Steppe and forest on the northern edge of the plain. Its people dig milkvetch root on the steppe and sell it to alchemists and physicians. A Wood vein in the forest gives a sweet dew on its leaves at dawn.

prov_r14_8.name: Tầm Dược
prov_r14_8.lore: High forest, mountain and plain in the west, more than fourteen hundred metres up. Its people gather mountain herbs on the forested slopes. A Wood vein high in the forest and a realgar mine in the rock lie above the village.

prov_r14_9.name: Xảo Tượng
prov_r14_9.lore: Forest, high plain and mountain north-west of the Pivot's mountain. Its people are carpenters who work the mountain timber into beams, carts and array frames for the plain. A warm spring on the mountain is where they rest their aching backs.

prov_cung_tinh_lake_1.name: Phong Văn Hồ
prov_cung_tinh_lake_1.look: A small, shallow lake on the high plain just west of Tinh Lạc Hồ, its surface always wrinkled by the wind.
prov_cung_tinh_lake_1.lore: Unlike its neighbour it holds no stars, for the wind never lets it lie still. Củng Tinh's novices are sent to watch it first, to learn what a broken reflection looks like.

prov_p140_beast_lair_1.name: Thiết Đề Nguyên
prov_p140_beast_lair_1.look: Open steppe beyond the incense groves, beaten bare in long tracks by a running herd.
prov_p140_beast_lair_1.lore: A herd of wild spirit horses with hooves hard as iron runs here and tramples anything in its way. Mộc Hương's woodcutters stay inside the groves when they hear it.

prov_p141_spirit_vein_1.name: Bàn Căn Mạch
prov_p141_spirit_vein_1.look: A dip in the steppe where great roots break the surface in coils, though no tree stands near.
prov_p141_spirit_vein_1.lore: Its qi (linh khí) runs to Earth and Wood. The villagers of Thụ Âm say these are the roots of their great tree, and that the tree drinks from the vein.

prov_p141_ruin_2.name: Khô Tỉnh Trấn
prov_p141_ruin_2.look: Mud-brick walls on the steppe around a deep stone well, dry to the bottom, with empty houses roofless around it.
prov_p141_ruin_2.lore: A caravan halt that grew into a town around its well from 530. The well failed in the drought of 940, and the people left for the river.

prov_p52_peak_1.name: Thạch Quyền Phong
prov_p52_peak_1.look: A squat, flat-topped mountain above the market, shaped like the weight of a steelyard.
prov_p52_peak_1.lore: The market's weighers say it is the counterweight that keeps the heart in balance. Its qi runs to Earth.

prov_p52_mine_2.name: Hoàng Đồng Khoáng
prov_p52_mine_2.look: A small mine of brassy, glittering ore high on the mountain, with a casting shed at the path's foot.
prov_p52_mine_2.lore: Its copper is cast into the bronze weights of Thiên Quyền Thị. A weight cast here is tested against the standard before it leaves the shed.

prov_p81_spirit_vein_1.name: Kiều Cơ Mạch
prov_p81_spirit_vein_1.look: A low swell of steppe where bare grey bedrock breaks through the grass in smooth domes.
prov_p81_spirit_vein_1.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, solid and slow. The builders of Thạch Kiều's bridge are said to have cut its first stones here.

prov_p81_ruin_2.name: Minh Sa Các
prov_p81_ruin_2.look: The roof ridge of a pavilion standing out of a dune on the desert edge, its halls filled with sand to the eaves.
prov_p81_ruin_2.lore: A small sect that studied the humming of the dunes was founded here in 560. The dunes crept over its halls for three centuries, and in 893 its last disciples gave up digging and went to Thạch Kiều.

prov_thien_xu_peak_1.name: Xu Trụ Phong
prov_thien_xu_peak_1.look: A sheer pillar of grey rock above the seat's terraces, green with moss to a height no moss should reach.
prov_thien_xu_peak_1.lore: It stands over Tử Vi Mạch inside the blessed land, and its qi runs to Metal and Earth. Only the Pivot's elders may meditate on its summit.

prov_thien_xu_mine_2.name: Trận Thạch Khoáng
prov_thien_xu_mine_2.look: A neat quarry below the lowest hall, its walls cut in square steps, with round stone blanks stacked for carving.
prov_thien_xu_mine_2.lore: The stone for the Pivot's array discs is cut here, close-grained and heavy with the blessed land's qi. Each blank is weighed at Thiên Quyền Thị before it is carved.

prov_r14_1_village_1.name: Hồng Quả Thôn
prov_r14_1_village_1.look: A forest-edge village of grey roofs among hawthorn hedges red with berries in autumn.
prov_r14_1_village_1.lore: Its people make hawthorn sweets and medicine for the markets of Thiên Quyền. Children are paid in candied berries for picking.

prov_r14_1_spirit_vein_2.name: Thái Bạch Mạch
prov_r14_1_spirit_vein_2.gloss: Vein of the Great White Star
prov_r14_1_spirit_vein_2.look: A pale band of white quartz across a bare mountain face, bright in the evening light.
prov_r14_1_spirit_vein_2.lore: Named for the evening star, its qi runs to Metal. Sword cultivators of the plain come to temper their blades on it.

prov_r14_10_spirit_vein_1.name: Địa Hỏa Mạch
prov_r14_10_spirit_vein_1.look: Cracked badland ground that steams in the cold and is warm to the hand.
prov_r14_10_spirit_vein_1.lore: Its qi runs to Fire. The sulphur workers of Lưu Hoàng say its heat is why the pans never freeze.

prov_r14_11_hot_spring_1.name: Đan Nhũ Thang
prov_r14_11_hot_spring_1.look: A warm, milky-red pool in a steppe hollow below the cinnabar terraces.
prov_r14_11_hot_spring_1.lore: Miners of Thần Sa wash the red dust off here after each shift. Alchemists warn them not to drink it.

prov_r14_12_village_1.name: Thanh Khoa Thôn
prov_r14_12_village_1.look: Flat-roofed stone houses on the river, with barley fields and yaks grazing the far bank.
prov_r14_12_village_1.lore: Its people grow highland barley and roast it into flour, and send yak butter up to the Pivot's kitchens. They are the highest farmers on the plain.

prov_r14_12_lake_2.name: Bán Nguyệt Hồ
prov_r14_12_lake_2.look: A crescent-shaped lake just east of Tinh Lạc Hồ, its reedy shallows full of nesting geese.
prov_r14_12_lake_2.lore: It is fed by the overflow of Tinh Lạc Hồ and is too reedy to hold the stars. Thanh Khoa's people cut its reeds for thatch.

prov_r14_12_mine_3.name: Tinh Kính Khoáng
prov_r14_12_mine_3.look: A high cut in bare mountain rock, glittering with clear crystal, at the edge of the seat's warded slopes.
prov_r14_12_mine_3.lore: Rock crystal from here is ground into lenses and array crystals for the Pivot's formation masters and for the armillary of Củng Tinh Quán.

prov_r14_12_ruin_4.name: Tây Quan Bảo
prov_r14_12_ruin_4.look: Tumbled stone walls across a forested saddle on the seat's west road, with an empty gate arch standing alone.
prov_r14_12_ruin_4.lore: It guarded the west road to the seat from 340 and held it through the War of the Pivot. After the Compact was set the garrison stood down in 520, and its stones were carried off to build Thanh Khoa.

prov_r14_12_minor_seat_p.name: Hoa Cái Đường
prov_r14_12_minor_seat_p.look: A compact hall of dark stone on a forested shoulder below the seat, its chimneys trailing thin coloured smoke from the furnaces within.
prov_r14_12_minor_seat_p.lore: Pill refiners (luyện đan) who use the cinnabar and sulphur of the red badlands founded this hall in 1060 under Thiên Xu, naming it for the canopy of stars over the pole. Its pills are sold through Thiên Quyền Thị and weighed there like everything else.

sect.name: Hoa Cái Đường
sect.craft: pill refining (luyện đan) from badland cinnabar and sulphur

prov_r14_13_village_1.name: Khung Lư Thôn
prov_r14_13_village_1.look: A ring of white felt yurts on the steppe, with horses tethered between them and dung fires smoking.
prov_r14_13_village_1.lore: Its herders move with the grass and come back here each winter. The village is wherever the yurts stand, but it always returns to the same ring of stones.

prov_r14_13_hot_spring_2.name: Dương Hòa Tuyền
prov_r14_13_hot_spring_2.look: A warm, clear spring in a sheltered hollow of the hills, ringed with green grass in the depth of winter.
prov_r14_13_hot_spring_2.lore: The yurt herders winter beside it. Lambs born near it are said never to take cold.

prov_r14_13_ruin_3.name: Khuy Thiên Các
prov_r14_13_ruin_3.look: A roofless stone tower on a mountain shoulder, with a stair spiralling up to an empty platform open to the sky.
prov_r14_13_ruin_3.lore: Star-readers founded it in 380, rivals of Củng Tinh Quán. In 650 its head went blind, and its disciples joined the abbey and carried their charts with them; the tower has stood empty since.

prov_r14_14_peak_1.name: Tùng Ảnh Phong
prov_r14_14_peak_1.look: A forested peak whose pines throw long shadows across the plain at sunset.
prov_r14_14_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herders on the plain tell the hour by how far its shadow has run.

prov_r14_14_mine_2.name: Kim Sa Khoáng
prov_r14_14_mine_2.look: Wooden sluices in a mountain stream, with gold-washers bent over pans in the cold water.
prov_r14_14_mine_2.lore: Gold is washed from the stream gravel in summer. Every washer pays a tenth to the Pivot by weight at Thiên Quyền.

prov_r14_15_peak_1.name: Cửu Diệu Phong
prov_r14_15_peak_1.look: A tall grey peak south of the seat with nine rock knobs around its summit.
prov_r14_15_peak_1.lore: The Pivot's disciples go there to sit alone. Its qi runs to Metal.

prov_r14_15_mine_2.name: Thiết Sa Khoáng
prov_r14_15_mine_2.look: Black sand washed in a mountain gully and heaped on hide sheets to dry.
prov_r14_15_mine_2.lore: Iron sand from here is carried up to the seat's smithies and smelted for the sect's tools.

prov_r14_16_peak_1.name: Câu Trần Phong
prov_r14_16_peak_1.look: A low, curved ridge-peak bending like a hook above the steppe.
prov_r14_16_peak_1.lore: Named for the star group that curls around the pole. Its qi runs to Earth.

prov_r14_16_ruin_2.name: Phong Toại Bảo
prov_r14_16_ruin_2.look: A small stone fort on a mountain spur, its beacon tower still standing with a blackened fire basket on top.
prov_r14_16_ruin_2.lore: From 505 its beacon passed warnings from the borders to the seat. After the truce of 805 the Pivot stood down its beacon line, and the fort was left in 806.

prov_r14_17_peak_1.name: Mã An Phong
prov_r14_17_peak_1.look: A double-humped peak on the steppe with a deep saddle between its summits, where the caravan path crosses.
prov_r14_17_peak_1.lore: Caravans between Thiên Quyền and the southern mines cross its saddle. Its qi runs to Earth.

prov_r14_18_peak_1.name: Xa Luân Phong
prov_r14_18_peak_1.look: A round-topped peak ringed by a circle of rock ribs like the spokes of a wheel.
prov_r14_18_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Herders say the five chariots of the sky rest on it.

prov_r14_18_mine_2.name: Đới Văn Khoáng
prov_r14_18_mine_2.look: Banded agate nodules broken from grey mountain rock and sorted into baskets by colour.
prov_r14_18_mine_2.lore: Agate from here is cut into beads and seals at Thạch Kiều.

prov_r14_18_ruin_3.name: Truân Điền Trại
prov_r14_18_ruin_3.look: Low stone walls around overgrown fields in a grassy valley, with a ruined barracks along one side.
prov_r14_18_ruin_3.lore: Soldier-farmers held it from 290, growing their own grain while they watched the south. After the Compact of 510 the Pivot no longer paid them, and by 530 the last had gone to Thạch Kiều.

prov_r14_19_peak_1.name: Hồi Thủ Phong
prov_r14_19_peak_1.look: A lonely peak on the steppe rim from which the whole plain can be seen behind and the grey waste ahead.
prov_r14_19_peak_1.lore: Soldiers going west to Cố Lũy are said to have looked back at the plain from here. Its qi runs to Metal.

prov_r14_19_ruin_2.name: Lang Yên Trại
prov_r14_19_ruin_2.look: A ring of tumbled stones on a mountain flank with a heap of scorched signal stones at its centre.
prov_r14_19_ruin_2.lore: An outpost of Cố Lũy's line from 795, where signal smoke was lit to warn the ramparts. After the battle of 803 no one came to relieve it, and it was abandoned at the truce of 805.

prov_r14_2_peak_1.name: Thứu Chủy Phong
prov_r14_2_peak_1.look: A hooked rock beak jutting from a forested mountain.
prov_r14_2_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Bark peelers use it to find their way back to their camps.

prov_r14_20_peak_1.name: Tê Mã Phong
prov_r14_20_peak_1.look: A bare steppe peak above the grey edge of the waste, its rocks scoured by wind.
prov_r14_20_peak_1.lore: Herders say they hear horses neighing from it on still nights, as others hear them in the miasma. Its qi runs to Earth.

prov_r14_20_mine_2.name: Bạch Phàn Khoáng
prov_r14_20_mine_2.look: White-crusted pits in grey mountain rock, with crystals drying in shallow trays.
prov_r14_20_mine_2.lore: Alum from here fixes dyes and stops bleeding. The day crews leave before dusk and never sleep on the ridge.

prov_r14_21_village_1.name: Mao Ngưu Thôn
prov_r14_21_village_1.look: Low stone houses with yak-hair tent roofs on the open high plain, the yaks grazing up to the doors.
prov_r14_21_village_1.lore: Its herders keep yaks and sheep on the short grass near Cố Lũy. They leave a bowl of butter on the old ramparts each spring.

prov_r14_21_hot_spring_2.name: Tẩy Giáp Trì
prov_r14_21_hot_spring_2.look: A steaming pool in a fold of the high plain, its rim of rust-stained stones.
prov_r14_21_hot_spring_2.lore: Quý Trường Kích's soldiers washed their armour here in the five years they held Cố Lũy. Herders say the rust in its stones is theirs.

prov_r14_22_village_1.name: Tô Du Thôn
prov_r14_22_village_1.look: Stone houses on the river with butter churns at every door and cheese drying on the roofs.
prov_r14_22_village_1.lore: Its herders make yak butter and cheese and carry them to Thạch Kiều. Butter tea is offered to every traveller, and it is rude to refuse a third bowl.

prov_r14_22_spirit_vein_2.name: Thổ Long Mạch
prov_r14_22_spirit_vein_2.look: A long ochre ridge of badland winding beside the river like a sleeping beast.
prov_r14_22_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. The herders will not dig into it.

prov_r14_22_mine_3.name: Thanh Kim Khoáng
prov_r14_22_mine_3.look: A narrow adit in grey mountain rock, the spoil flecked with deep blue stone.
prov_r14_22_mine_3.lore: Lapis from here is ground into the blue of the Pivot's star charts.

prov_r14_22_ruin_4.name: Lão Mã Bảo
prov_r14_22_ruin_4.look: Long stone stables and a walled yard on the high plain, empty but for grass and wind.
prov_r14_22_ruin_4.lore: The Pivot bred remounts for its riders here from 600. After the battle of 803 no riders came back to claim the horses; the herds were sold and the fort was left by 806.

prov_r14_23_village_1.name: Thạch Ốc Thôn
prov_r14_23_village_1.look: Thick-walled stone houses huddled on a river bend, with barley and pea fields on the flats.
prov_r14_23_village_1.lore: Its houses are built of stone against the plateau wind. Each house keeps one stone from the falling stars of the Wild Age in its wall, or says it does.

prov_r14_23_spirit_vein_2.name: Lưu Tinh Mạch
prov_r14_23_spirit_vein_2.look: A shallow dish in the steppe, its rocks scorched black and glassy.
prov_r14_23_spirit_vein_2.lore: Said to be where one of the stones of the nine days struck, its qi runs to Metal. Củng Tinh's star-readers visit it each year.

prov_r14_23_mine_3.name: Đại Giả Khoáng
prov_r14_23_mine_3.look: A badland slope dug into red-brown terraces, with ochre cakes drying in rows.
prov_r14_23_mine_3.lore: Its ochre is used for paint and in medicine. The diggers' hands stay red for a season.

prov_r14_24_village_1.name: Xa Ngưu Thôn
prov_r14_24_village_1.look: Stone cattle pens and low houses on the steppe, with herds dust-brown on the slopes.
prov_r14_24_village_1.lore: Its people raise oxen for the caravans and the Pivot's carts. An ox from here is sold with its weight written on its horn.

prov_r14_24_spirit_vein_2.name: Cương Phong Mạch
prov_r14_24_spirit_vein_2.look: A bare steppe shoulder high above the river where the wind never stops and the grass grows flat.
prov_r14_24_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, sharp as the wind. Cultivators sit here to hone their spirit sense.

prov_r14_24_mine_3.name: Tử Thạch Khoáng
prov_r14_24_mine_3.look: Purple crystal geodes cracked open in a mountain cut.
prov_r14_24_mine_3.lore: Amethyst from here is set into the Pivot's ceremonial seals.

prov_r14_25_village_1.name: Hồ Dương Thôn
prov_r14_25_village_1.look: A river village under gnarled desert poplars gold in autumn, with salt pans by the bank.
prov_r14_25_village_1.lore: Its people farm the river flats and boil salt from the warm brine spring in the hills. Caravans bound for the desert water here.

prov_r14_25_hot_spring_2.name: Bạch Diêm Tuyền
prov_r14_25_hot_spring_2.look: A warm brine spring on the steppe, crusted with white salt around its rim.
prov_r14_25_hot_spring_2.lore: Hồ Dương's people boil its brine for salt. The salt is weighed at Thạch Kiều and sold across the heart.

prov_r14_26_peak_1.name: Thủ Linh Phong
prov_r14_26_peak_1.gloss: Peak of the Vigil for the Dead
prov_r14_26_peak_1.look: A dark mountain standing over the grey waste, its foot lost in haze.
prov_r14_26_peak_1.lore: Thiên Xu's patrols climb it to look over Chiết Kích Nguyên without entering it. Its qi runs to Earth, heavy and dark.

prov_r14_27_village_1.name: Thạch Điền Thôn
prov_r14_27_village_1.look: Tiny stone-walled terraces stepping up a high slope, with a village of flat roofs at their foot.
prov_r14_27_village_1.lore: Its people farm barley in walled terraces and keep goats. Every stone in the walls was cleared from the fields by hand.

prov_r14_27_hot_spring_2.name: Hoàng Yên Tuyền
prov_r14_27_hot_spring_2.look: A sulphurous spring in red badland, wrapped in yellow steam.
prov_r14_27_hot_spring_2.lore: It smells of eggs and heals the skin. The goatherds bathe their flocks in its runoff against mites.

prov_r14_27_mine_3.name: Tập Trận Khoáng
prov_r14_27_mine_3.look: A soft grey soapstone pit on the high plain, its walls smooth and greasy to the touch.
prov_r14_27_mine_3.lore: Soapstone from here is carved into bowls and into the practice array discs of novice formation masters.

prov_r14_28_village_1.name: Bách Linh Thôn
prov_r14_28_village_1.look: A steppe village on the river, its fields loud with larks in spring.
prov_r14_28_village_1.lore: Its people herd sheep and farm the river flats. Lark cages hang at every door, and a good singer is worth a sheep.

prov_r14_28_spirit_vein_2.name: Tảo Xuân Mạch
prov_r14_28_spirit_vein_2.look: A forested fold of the hills where the leaves come out a month before anywhere else.
prov_r14_28_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herders bring sick lambs here in early spring.

prov_r14_28_mine_3.name: Ngân Sa Khoáng
prov_r14_28_mine_3.look: Glittering grey sand dug from a mountain pocket and washed in leather troughs.
prov_r14_28_mine_3.lore: The silver sand is sent to the Pivot's mint. Washers are searched at the gate each night.

prov_r14_29_village_1.name: Thạch Dương Thôn
prov_r14_29_village_1.look: A cluster of stone huts on high stony steppe with goats on every rock.
prov_r14_29_village_1.lore: Its herders keep goats under the hawk cliffs. They say the grey hawks take only the goats that stray.

prov_r14_29_mine_2.name: Lục Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r14_29_mine_2.look: A cut in a high mountain face showing veins of dark green stone.
prov_r14_29_mine_2.lore: Green jade from here is carved at Bích Khê and sold back to the plain at twice the price.

prov_r14_3_peak_1.name: Bạch Trâm Phong
prov_r14_3_peak_1.look: A thin, pale spire of rock standing above the forest and the morning cloud.
prov_r14_3_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. It can be seen from Mộc Hương Thôn on clear days.

prov_r14_30_village_1.name: Mã Nãi Thôn
prov_r14_30_village_1.look: Felt and stone houses by the river, with leather bags of fermenting milk hanging from posts.
prov_r14_30_village_1.lore: Its herders brew fermented mare's milk and trade it at Thạch Kiều. A guest is offered a bowl before a word is spoken.

prov_r14_30_spirit_vein_2.name: Quảng Dã Mạch
prov_r14_30_spirit_vein_2.look: A broad, gently rising stretch of steppe where the grass grows waist-high.
prov_r14_30_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. Horses grazed on it grow strong and steady.

prov_r14_31_peak_1.name: Thạch Chung Phong
prov_r14_31_peak_1.look: A bell-shaped peak of grey rock above the ruined city.
prov_r14_31_peak_1.lore: Its rocks ring when struck. Its qi runs to Metal.

prov_r14_31_ruin_2.name: Lục Hợp Thành
prov_r14_31_ruin_2.look: Long walls and a grid of empty streets on a mountain shelf, with a cracked stone cistern at the centre.
prov_r14_31_ruin_2.lore: A caravan city built on the southern road in 330, under Thiên Xu's protection. In 912 an earthquake split its cistern and dried its springs, and within a year its people had moved to Thạch Kiều.

prov_r14_32_beast_lair_1.name: Kim Hạt Cốc
prov_r14_32_beast_lair_1.look: A shallow sandy valley in the steppe, its sand ridged by the tracks of many legs.
prov_r14_32_beast_lair_1.lore: Golden spirit scorpions as big as dogs bury themselves here. Their venom is prized by alchemists, and their hunters seldom grow old.

prov_r14_33_village_1.name: Du Mục Thôn
prov_r14_33_village_1.look: A winter camp of stone-walled yurts on the steppe, with dung stacked high against the walls.
prov_r14_33_village_1.lore: Herders who move with the grass all summer winter here. The camp's stone walls are older than anyone can remember.

prov_r14_33_hot_spring_2.name: Đông Noãn Tuyền
prov_r14_33_hot_spring_2.look: A steaming spring among rocks on the steppe, warm enough to bathe in during snow.
prov_r14_33_hot_spring_2.lore: The nomads winter by it and bathe in it on New Year's night.

prov_r14_33_mine_3.name: Tiêu Thạch Khoáng
prov_r14_33_mine_3.look: A cave in the mountain whose walls are crusted with white salt, scraped into sacks.
prov_r14_33_mine_3.lore: Saltpetre from here is sold to Thiên Xu for fire powders, mixed with the sulphur of Lưu Hoàng.

prov_r14_34_village_1.name: Liệp Ưng Thôn
prov_r14_34_village_1.look: A steppe village of stone houses with hooded hawks on perches at every door.
prov_r14_34_village_1.lore: Its people fly hawks and falcons for hares and foxes and sell trained birds at Thạch Kiều.

prov_r14_34_peak_2.name: Sương Đầu Phong
prov_r14_34_peak_2.look: A high mountain whose summit stays white with frost and snow most of the year.
prov_r14_34_peak_2.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Falconers release their old birds from its slopes.

prov_r14_35_peak_1.name: Thọ Tinh Phong
prov_r14_35_peak_1.look: A tall, broad peak on the southern rim, its summit catching the light of the southern sky.
prov_r14_35_peak_1.lore: Old cultivators climb it near the end of their years to watch the longevity star. Its qi runs to Earth.

prov_r14_35_mine_2.name: Hồng Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r14_35_mine_2.look: A few narrow adits in a high mountain face, red grains glinting in the spoil.
prov_r14_35_mine_2.lore: Rubies are dug here in summer by small crews. The best go to the Pivot; the rest to Thạch Kiều.

prov_r14_36_peak_1.name: Lục Bình Phong
prov_r14_36_peak_1.look: A grassy-topped mountain whose long green summit looks out over the coast.
prov_r14_36_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Wood and Earth. From its summit the far water can be seen.

prov_r14_36_mine_2.name: Hải Lam Khoáng
prov_r14_36_mine_2.look: Blue-stained rock in a mountain cut above the coast, with ore crushed and washed in a stream.
prov_r14_36_mine_2.lore: Azurite from here gives copper and the blue paint of the Pivot's halls.

prov_r14_4_village_1.name: Tùng Nhân Thôn
prov_r14_4_village_1.look: A forest-edge village with sacks of pine cones heaped by every door and sheep on the steppe beyond.
prov_r14_4_village_1.lore: Its people gather pine nuts in autumn and herd sheep the rest of the year.

prov_r14_4_peak_2.name: Liên Hoa Phong
prov_r14_4_peak_2.look: A ring of rock petals around a central summit north of the seat's mountains.
prov_r14_4_peak_2.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. Travellers from the north see it first of all the seat's mountains.

prov_r14_5_village_1.name: Đương Quy Thôn
prov_r14_5_village_1.look: A forest village on a high slope, with angelica beds and roots drying on bamboo trays.
prov_r14_5_village_1.lore: Its people grow and dig angelica root for the alchemists of the plain. A root that grows forked is given to a newly married couple.

prov_r14_5_peak_2.name: Tiên Nhân Phong
prov_r14_5_peak_2.look: A forested peak topped by a rock shaped like a seated figure.
prov_r14_5_peak_2.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Villagers leave food at the rock for the immortal they say sits there.

prov_r14_5_mine_3.name: Huyền Cương Khoáng
prov_r14_5_mine_3.look: A dark adit in mountain rock with heaps of black, heavy ore at its mouth.
prov_r14_5_mine_3.lore: Its dark iron-manganese ore is smelted into tough black steel for tools.

prov_r14_6_peak_1.name: Thái Nhất Phong
prov_r14_6_peak_1.look: A sharp high peak north of the seat, lined up with the pole star at night.
prov_r14_6_peak_1.lore: The Pivot's watchmen keep a post on its shoulder. Its qi runs to Metal.

prov_r14_6_mine_2.name: Kim Tinh Khoáng
prov_r14_6_mine_2.look: A small, guarded adit in bare mountain rock, its mouth closed with an iron grille.
prov_r14_6_mine_2.lore: Gold is dug here for the sect's own use, and its output is not weighed in the market.

prov_r14_7_village_1.name: Hoàng Kỳ Thôn
prov_r14_7_village_1.look: A village at the forest edge with bundles of yellow root drying on the eaves.
prov_r14_7_village_1.lore: Its people dig milkvetch root on the steppe and sell it to physicians and alchemists.

prov_r14_7_spirit_vein_2.name: Cam Lộ Mạch
prov_r14_7_spirit_vein_2.look: A forest glade where a sweet dew beads on the leaves every dawn.
prov_r14_7_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Children lick the leaves in spring, and the alchemists collect the dew in jars.

prov_r14_8_village_1.name: Tầm Dược Thôn
prov_r14_8_village_1.look: A high forest village of log houses with baskets of herbs hung from every beam.
prov_r14_8_village_1.lore: Its people climb the forested slopes for mountain herbs. They rope themselves together on the steep ground.

prov_r14_8_spirit_vein_2.name: Bách Tuế Mạch
prov_r14_8_spirit_vein_2.look: A stand of enormous old trees high in the forest, the ground soft with centuries of needles.
prov_r14_8_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herb gatherers say a plant that grows here lives a hundred years.

prov_r14_8_mine_3.name: Tị Xà Khoáng
prov_r14_8_mine_3.look: Orange-red realgar crystals in grey mountain rock, broken out and wrapped in leaves.
prov_r14_8_mine_3.lore: Realgar from here is used against snakes and in some pills. The miners do not eat where they dig.

prov_r14_9_village_1.name: Xảo Tượng Thôn
prov_r14_9_village_1.look: A forest village of fine timber houses with carved beams and workshops full of shavings.
prov_r14_9_village_1.lore: Its carpenters make beams, carts and array frames for the plain. The Pivot's formation masters order their frames here.

prov_r14_9_hot_spring_2.name: Tẩy Tâm Tuyền
prov_r14_9_hot_spring_2.look: A clear warm spring in a mountain cleft, its water so still it seems not to move.
prov_r14_9_hot_spring_2.lore: Carpenters rest their backs here. Cultivators say it calms the heart before a breakthrough.
